item.title: Advancing Food Quality and Sustainable Food Systems through Post-Harvest Innovations, Cold Chains, and Digital Technologies
item.content:encoded:
Harshad Sonar, Indian Institute of Management (IIM)

Bishal Dey Sarkar, Indian Institute of Management (IIM)

Joash Mageto, University of Johannesburg

Samuel Fosso Wamba, TBS Education

This special issue addresses how post-harvest innovations, cold-chain operations, and digital technologies can enhance food quality and sustainability across supply chains. The editors recognize that food losses stem from interconnected operational and infrastructural challenges, particularly in developing economies. The call seeks integrated research that connects previously separate topics to understand how innovations work together to improve food system outcomes.

The issue welcomes interdisciplinary contributions examining how post-harvest innovations, cold-chain strategies, digital technologies like AI and blockchain, and collaborative governance can reduce waste, improve transparency, and build resilient food systems. Research should prioritize food-centric outcomes and provide actionable insights for researchers, policymakers, producers, and stakeholders developing safer and more sustainable food systems.

Appel publié par British Food Journal. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Post-harvest management for food quality preservation and food loss reduction
  • Cold chain management for food safety, nutritional quality, and perishability
  • Digital technologies for food quality, traceability, and transparency
  • Smart packaging and innovative food preservation technologies
  • Sustainable and resilient food systems under climate and supply chain disruptions
  • Food waste reduction, circular food systems, and resource-efficient post-harvest practices
  • Food safety governance, regulatory compliance, and stakeholder collaboration
  • Data-driven decision making and policy innovations for sustainable food security

Timeline

  • January 9, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • February 28, 2027: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Celebrating (over) 125 years of the British Food Journal
item.content:encoded:
The British Food Journal is inviting submissions for its ongoing publication series, marking over 125 years of contributions to food-related research. The journal has published a bibliometric analysis examining its publication history, thematic developments, and impact on food research and society throughout its long history.

Authors are encouraged to submit articles through ScholarOne Manuscripts to contribute to the journal's future. All submissions must adhere to Emerald Publishing Author Guidelines and align with the journal's aims and scope in food-related research.

item.title: Origin-Linked Foods in Contemporary Markets: Authenticity, Trust, Traceability and Sustainable Value Creation
item.content:encoded:
Hiram Ting, Asia Pacific University of Technology and Innovation

Ziyi Gao, Yunnan University of Finance and Economics

Zhengxin Li, Tsinghua University

Jungyun Hur, California State University, Sacramento

Rawan Nimri, Griffith University

Alicia Orea-Giner, Universidad Rey Juan Carlos

Origin-linked foods—including geographical indications, protected designations of origin, regional specialties, and heritage foods—operate as quality cues, collective brands, and territorial-development resources. While these systems are substantial across Europe, China, Mexico and the United States, significant research questions remain about how origin claims become credible and valuable to consumers and markets.

This special issue investigates three interconnected dimensions: how consumers understand and value origin authenticity; how certification and traceability systems govern markets and verify provenance; and how the resulting benefits and risks are distributed among producers, processors, retailers and places. The call welcomes empirical, conceptual and review articles using diverse methodologies, with particular interest in work from underrepresented regions.

Appel publié par British Food Journal. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Consumer understanding of geographical indications and origin labels
  • Origin cues and brand authenticity
  • Willingness to pay and food-system trust
  • Interactions among origin, price, quality, safety, sustainability and health claims
  • Storytelling and cultural meaning in authenticity claims
  • GI/PDO/PGI certification systems as collective brands
  • Traceability and provenance verification
  • Food fraud and counterfeiting
  • Digital certificates, QR codes and blockchain verification
  • Producer coordination and supply-chain governance
  • Price premium distribution along value chains
  • Rural livelihoods and cultural knowledge
  • Biodiversity and environmental sustainability
  • Scaling and standardisation
  • Digital platforms and e-commerce
  • Cross-border markets
  • Wild and foraged foods

Timeline

  • October 1, 2026: Opening date for manuscript submissions
  • May 31, 2027: Closing date for manuscript submissions

item.title: Alternative Proteins for Sustainable and Ethical Food Systems: Consumer, Production, and Supply-Chain Perspectives
item.content:encoded:
The global food system is undergoing profound transformation driven by growing concerns about climate change, biodiversity loss, animal welfare, public health, and the long-term sustainability of livestock-based production models. Against this backdrop, alternative proteins, including cultured meat, plant-based meat analogues, insect-based products and novel dairy substitutes, have emerged as promising pathways for addressing environmental pressures while meeting evolving consumer expectations for ethical, healthy and sustainable diets. Although consumer research on these products has expanded rapidly, a comprehensive understanding of how alternative proteins reshape the broader agrifood system remains limited. Existing studies often address consumption, production, regulation, and socio-cultural dynamics in isolation, leaving significant knowledge gaps regarding value-chain restructuring, producer adoption, economic feasibility, and governance.

Appel publié par British Food Journal. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Consumer acceptance, preferences, and willingness to pay for alternative meats and dairy products
  • Farm-level decision-making and economic feasibility of adopting alternative-protein production systems
  • Sustainability, environmental and life-cycle assessments of alternative protein supply chains
  • Regulatory frameworks, certification, labelling, and standards for emerging protein products
  • Cultural, ethical, and societal narratives shaping acceptance and legitimacy
  • Communication, trust-building, and transparency strategies across the supply chain

Timeline

  • November 30, 2026: Closing date for manuscript submissions
